checkedAlternates.risk: A standing penguin hides its legs, and a swimming one reads as legless.
checkedAlternates.resolution: Penguins walk on two legs, which is visible in any familiar image of one on land.

checkedAlternates.risk: Players who lump spiders in with insects may reach for a different count.
checkedAlternates.resolution: A spider has eight legs; insect or arachnid, both counts are above four, so the group holds either way.

checkedAlternates.risk: Scorpions are less familiar than the other three in their group and the pincers can be miscounted as legs.
checkedAlternates.resolution: Eight walking legs, and the group only asks for more than four, so an imprecise count still lands correctly.

authorReview.notes: Every group is a plain leg count, so a wrong answer means a wrong fact rather than a second valid reading.

blindPlaytest.notes: Watch whether the two-legged row reads as "birds" instead of "two legs"; ostrich and penguin are both birds, which is a coincidence of this item set, not the rule.
